note.headline: Yen jump and copper bid pull risk gauge to neutral while breadth fails
note.standfirst: A 1.70% yen rally and a 1.38% copper bid did more work on the risk barometer than the S&P's 0.38% decline, while decliners outnumbered advancers by nearly three to one. Positioning into tomorrow should track USD/JPY and the front end of the Treasury curve, not index levels that undersell how narrow this market has become.
takeaways: Breadth failed even as headline indices barely moved: 7 advancers against 19 decliners, a ratio of 0.37.
USD/JPY's 1.70% move was the single largest input to the risk barometer at -3.0, more than three times any other driver.
Treasury yields fell across the curve, led by the front end (2-year down 5bp to 4.34%), widening 2s10s by 3bp to 43bp.
AI infrastructure names diverged sharply from mega-cap software and consumer names: AMD rose 4.69% and Oracle rose 3.08% against Tesla down 5.92% and Netflix down 5.35%.
note.desk_view:
Today confirms what the tape has been signaling for weeks: index levels overstate participation. The S&P fell 0.38% and the Dow fell 0.51%, but decliners beat advancers by nearly three to one and dispersion sits at 2.09. Nasdaq's 0.21% gain rode two names, AMD and Oracle, while the median stock lost ground. That gap between headline and breadth is now the central fact of the session, not a footnote to it.

The level that decides the next move sits in USD/JPY, not the S&P. Yen strength was the largest single input to the risk barometer at -3.0, more than three times the next-largest driver, and it came alongside Treasury yields falling across the curve: the 2-year down 5bp to 4.34%, the 10-year down 2bp to 4.77%, even as 2s10s widened to 43bp on front-end outperformance. Copper's 1.38% advance, the largest positive barometer input, is pulling the opposite direction. If the yen keeps bidding while copper keeps bidding too, that is not one signal, it is two markets pricing two different stories. Watch whether one gives way to the other before the open.
watching: Whether USD/JPY extends its 1.70% move or reverses it.
Whether 2s10s holds 43bp or the front end keeps outrunning the long end.
Credit spreads for confirmation: LQD and IEF are both sitting near recent lows.
Follow-through in AI infrastructure names after AMD's 4.69% and Oracle's 3.08% gains against a weak mega-cap software tape.
note.equities: Indices told four different stories. The Nasdaq 100 added 0.
